findings.where: formulas.after / script "TEXT with a date code, wrapped inside LEFT."
findings.issue: TEXT(A2,"mm") returns "03" on its own, so wrapping it in LEFT is redundant. Accountants in the comments will say so, and it costs a little credibility on an otherwise clean reel.
findings.fix: Either keep LEFT and add half a clause acknowledging it (the point is that LEFT now has characters to slice), or make the fix the shorter TEXT code and let the payoff carry the serial lesson.

findings.where: script line 3, caption "Two months of postings.\nI need a month column."
findings.issue: Column B already has a "Month" header on screen, so saying you need a month column reads slightly off against what the viewer sees.
findings.fix: Say you need the month broken out of the date, not that you need the column.

findings.issue: "46 where the month should be" is the same shape as 006 ("OPS where 12,480.00 was yesterday"). Still specific and fine, just the second time this construction runs.
findings.fix: Optional: try a phrasing that leads with the action, e.g. the value that lands when you pull the month off a date.

findings.where: script "03. That's the month, as real characters."
findings.issue: "as real characters" is a slightly technical tail for a spoken line.
findings.fix: Trim to something a controller would say out loud, e.g. "03. That's the actual month."

hook.note: Concrete symptom, six on-screen words, a number the viewer has actually seen in a month column. Loses a point only because the lead-plus-"where" construction has run before.

claims.claim: A date cell holds a serial number and the date shown is a number format on top of it
claims.note: Correct for Excel date values; the stored block matches (03/09/2026 = 46090).

claims.claim: LEFT(A2,2) returns the first two digits of the stored serial, not of the displayed date
claims.note: LEFT coerces the number to its general text form, ignoring the cell's number format.

claims.claim: Wrapping in TEXT produces characters LEFT can slice
claims.note: TEXT returns a text string, so LEFT operates on the formatted date.

claims.claim: "A number format changes what you see. It never changes what's stored."
claims.note: Accurate and correctly scoped to number formats, not to entered values.

claims.claim: Post copy: "using a date code that matches your regional settings"
claims.note: Correct caveat; TEXT format codes are locale-dependent, and narration stays vague enough not to overreach.
Matches the displayed dates in column A.

claims.claim: No function used requires a modern Excel version
claims.note: LEFT and TEXT exist in every supported build, so no version caveat is owed.
